title: Sr Manger External Affairs & Market Access
description: Senior Manager, External Affairs & Market Access – Benelux & Nordic Region Travel requirements: Up to 40% travel time – fluctuating with business requirements At Hologic, we are committed to improving and protecting women’s health. As Senior Manager, External Affairs & Market Access, you will be central to delivering on that commitment and to the success of the Benelux and Nordic region, where frequent guideline shifts, varying reimbursement maturity, complex tender dynamics, and diverse healthcare systems demand the highest clinical standards, while operating under significant budget constraints. We are looking for a strategic thinker with a strong commercial mindset who is resilient, action-oriented, and energized by building and executing strategy from the ground up. If you are passionate about Women’s Health and thrive in complexity, this is the role for you. Our ideal candidate is a Women’s Health leader who takes full ownership to shape the external environment and unlock access, advocating credibly with government parties, payers, and the wider healthcare ecosystem, while also driving internal alignment by “changing hearts and minds” and mobilizing teams behind clear priorities. As the reference point for Governmental Affairs and Policy Making, you will engage with government officials, industry associations, scientific societies, expert KOLs, and advocacy groups to influence policies, regulations, and guidelines, and you will deliver impact through disciplined execution and effective management of external partners and consultants. This is a highly differentiated opportunity across two regions, eight markets, six languages, and multiple healthcare systems. It is ideal for candidates who enjoy diversity, fast learning, and adapting strategies to local realities. The role is grounded in three areas: 1. Lead External Affairs by building a high-trust stakeholder network across ministries, payers, HTA bodies, regulators, associations, and scientific societies, and by converting those relationships into country- and business-specific strategies that influence the policy and funding environment. 2.
